title: Rigveda 7.90: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.90: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.90 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Vayu or Indra and Vayu. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 548v-549r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.90.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 548v
translation.original_text:
1pra vī̍ra̱yā śuca̍yo dadrire vām adhva̱ryubhi̱r madhu̍mantaḥ su̱tāsa̍ḥ | vaha̍ vāyo ni̱yuto̍ yā̱hy acchā̱ pibā̍ su̱tasyāndha̍so̱ madā̍ya ||
2ī̱śā̱nāya̱ prahu̍ti̱ṁ yas ta̱ āna̱ṭ chuci̱ṁ soma̍ṁ śucipā̱s tubhya̍ṁ vāyo | kṛ̱ṇoṣi̱ tam martye̍ṣu praśa̱staṁ jā̱to-jā̍to jāyate vā̱jy a̍sya ||
3rā̱ye nu yaṁ ja̱jñatū̱ roda̍sī̱me rā̱ye de̱vī dhi̱ṣaṇā̍ dhāti de̱vam | adha̍ vā̱yuṁ ni̱yuta̍ḥ saścata̱ svā u̱ta śve̱taṁ vasu̍dhitiṁ nire̱ke ||
4u̱cchann u̱ṣasa̍ḥ su̱dinā̍ ari̱prā u̱ru jyoti̍r vividu̱r dīdhyā̍nāḥ | gavya̍ṁ cid ū̱rvam u̱śijo̱ vi va̍vru̱s teṣā̱m anu̍ pra̱diva̍ḥ sasru̱r āpa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1To you pure juice, rich in meath, are offered by priest: through longing for the Pair of Heroes. Drive, Vâyu, bring thine harnessed horses hither: drink the pressed Soma till it make thee joyful.
2Whoso to thee, the Mighty, brings oblation, pure Soma unto thee, pure-drinking Vâyu, That man thou makest famous among mortals: to him strong sons are born in quick succession.
3The God whom both these worlds brought forth for riches, whom heavenly Dhishaṇâ for our wealth appointeth, His team of harnessed horses waits on Vâyu, and, foremost, on the radiant Treasure-bearer.
4The spotless Dawns with fair bright days have broken; they found the spacious light when they were shining. Eagerly they disclosed the stall of cattle: floods streamed for them as in the days aforetime.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 548v (numbered 69v by the scribe) (OPenn image 549, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.89.5 ‹-dharma yuyopima mā naḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 549r (numbered 70r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.90.5 ‹-sacante›. Verses 7.90.1-4 end on this page.

2īśānāya | pra-hutim | yaḥ | te | ānaṭ | śucim | somam | śuci-pāḥ | tubhyam | vāyo iti | kṛṇoṣi | tam | martyeṣu | pra-śastam | jātaḥ-jātaḥ | jāyate | vājyasya

translation.original_ref: RV 7.90.5-7 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 549r
translation.original_text:
5te sa̱tyena̱ mana̍sā̱ dīdhyā̍nā̱ḥ svena̍ yu̱ktāsa̱ḥ kratu̍nā vahanti | indra̍vāyū vīra̱vāha̱ṁ ratha̍ṁ vām īśā̱nayo̍r a̱bhi pṛkṣa̍ḥ sacante ||
6ī̱śā̱nāso̱ ye dadha̍te̱ sva̍r ṇo̱ gobhi̱r aśve̍bhi̱r vasu̍bhi̱r hira̍ṇyaiḥ | indra̍vāyū sū̱rayo̱ viśva̱m āyu̱r arva̍dbhir vī̱raiḥ pṛta̍nāsu sahyuḥ ||
7arva̍nto̱ na śrava̍so̱ bhikṣa̍māṇā indravā̱yū su̍ṣṭu̱tibhi̱r vasi̍ṣṭhāḥ | vā̱ja̱yanta̱ḥ sv ava̍se huvema yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
5These with their truthful spirit, shining brightly, move on provided with their natural insight. Viands attend the car that beareth Heroes, your car, ye Sovran Pair, Indra and Vâyu.
6May these who give us heavenly light, these rulers, with gifts of kine and horses, gold and treasures. These princes, through full life, Indra and Vâyu! o'ercome in battle with their steeds and heroes.
7Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasishṭhas, O Indra-Vâyu, with our fair laudations. Exerting all our power call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 549r (numbered 70r by the scribe) (OPenn image 549, lower leaf).
